title: Geometric stalks of closed direct image on algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Closed immersion means representable by closed immersions of schemes after every scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write $i_{\mathrm{et},*}$ for direct image of abelian sheaves under the induced morphism of small etale topoi [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. A geometric point is a map from the spectrum of an algebraically closed field, and its stalk is the colimit over pointed etale scheme neighbourhoods. For every abelian sheaf $A$ on $Z_{\mathrm{et}}$ and every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ factoring as $i\bar z$, the canonical restriction comparison is a natural isomorphism $$(i_{\mathrm{et},*}A)_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\bar z}.$$ For a geometric point $\bar x$ not factoring through $Z$, one has $(i_{\mathrm{et},*}A)_{\bar x}=0$. The comparison at $i\bar z$ sends the germ of a section on a pointed etale neighbourhood $U\to X$ to the germ of that same section on $U\times_X Z$ at the induced point, and is natural in $A$.

source.place: Tag 0DK1 (lemma-stalk-push-closed), with the corrected formula (i_*A)_{bar x}=A_{bar z}; Tag 04E5 (lemma-closed-immersion-push-pull), part (2), for vanishing on the complement. Scheme model: etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04FX (lemma-stalk-pushforward-closed-immersion).

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $p:U\to X$ from the algebraic-space definition. Choose a point $u$ above the image of $\bar x$. The specified-lift statement gives $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ with $p\bar u=\bar x$, over the original algebraically closed field. Set $D=U\times_X Z$ and write $k:D\hookrightarrow U$, $q:D\to Z$. By the representability hypothesis on $i$, $D$ is a scheme and $k$ is a closed immersion of schemes. The etale base-change statement makes $q$ etale. If $\bar x=i\bar z$, the pair $(\bar u,\bar z)$ defines $\bar d:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to D$. No finite-presentation hypothesis on the closed immersion and no finiteness condition on the atlas is needed.

source.place: Tag 0DK1 (lemma-stalk-push-closed), proof: choice of a pointed etale scheme neighbourhood; spaces-properties.tex Tag 05VN (lemma-geometric-lift-to-usual)

proof.text: Compute restriction of the direct image on this chart directly. For an etale scheme $T\to U$, it is etale over $X$ by etale composition, and $T\times_X Z=T\times_U D$. The definition of direct image along the base-change functor therefore gives $((i_*A)|_U)(T)=A(T\times_X Z)=(A|_D)(T\times_U D)=(k_*(A|_D))(T)$. Every fibre product here is a scheme: it is a base change of the representable closed immersion. Both restriction maps and a sheaf morphism $A\to B$ act by the same restriction maps or section homomorphisms on these expressions. Thus this is a natural identification of abelian sheaves on $U$, not an appeal to a module-only base-change theorem.

source.place: Tag 0DK1, proof, etale base change; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03LR (lemma-pushforward-etale-base-change), degree-zero formula

proof.text: Taking a stalk can be done after restriction to a fixed pointed etale scheme chart. Here is the colimit argument, for either $(U,\bar u)\to(X,\bar x)$ or $(D,\bar d)\to(Z,\bar z)$. Forgetting the chart structure sends pointed neighbourhoods over the chart to pointed neighbourhoods over the space. For a neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$ of the space, its fibre product with the chart, pointed by $(\bar w,\bar u)$ (respectively $(\bar w,\bar d)$), is terminal among chart-neighbourhoods equipped with a pointed map to $W$: the unique map to it is the pair of the given map and the chart structure map. These fibre products are etale schemes by representability and etale base change. Consequently cocones on sections over the chart extend uniquely to all neighbourhoods by restricting each section to that fibre product. Restricting back gives the original cocone by its compatibility with the two projections; the two extension operations are inverse. The colimit universal property gives $F_{\bar x}\cong(F|_U)_{\bar u}$ and, in the factoring case, $A_{\bar z}\cong(A|_D)_{\bar d}$. These maps send a section germ to its restriction germ. All categories are replaced by small skeletons in the fixed larger universe.

source.place: Tag 0DK1, proof: the stalk is unchanged on a pointed etale neighbourhood; explicit fibre-product verification of that assertion

proof.text: In the factoring case apply the scheme result to $k:D\hookrightarrow U$ and $\bar d$ from Step 1, with abelian sheaf $A|_D$. Its initiality assertion identifies the two colimits by the base-change comparison, giving $(k_*(A|_D))_{\bar u}\cong(A|_D)_{\bar d}$. Combine this with the section identity of Step 2 and the two stalk identifications of Step 3. A representative $s\in A(W\times_XZ)$ on $(W,\bar w)$ first restricts to $W\times_XU\times_XZ$; the scheme comparison takes its germ on that closed base change. Its image in $A_{\bar z}$ is exactly the germ of $s$ on $W\times_X Z$, because these two representatives differ by that pointed etale refinement. Thus the composite is the canonical restriction comparison required in the statement, and is an isomorphism of abelian groups.

source.place: Tag 0DK1 (lemma-stalk-push-closed), reduction to Tag 04FX (lemma-stalk-pushforward-closed-immersion); the scheme initiality and comparison are recorded in lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar

proof.text: If $\bar x$ does not factor through $Z$, then $\bar u$ does not factor through $D$. Its underlying point is outside the closed subset $|D|\subset U$: locally $D$ is cut out by an ideal, and a field-valued map whose image lies in its vanishing set kills that ideal and therefore factors. Let $U_0=U\setminus|D|$. This is an open scheme neighbourhood of $\bar u$, etale over $U$ by the open-immersion statement. For every etale $T\to U_0$, $T\times_U D=\varnothing$, so the section formula of Step 2 gives $(k_*(A|_D))(T)=A(\varnothing)=0$. The last equality follows from the sheaf equalizer axiom for the empty covering of the empty scheme: the empty product of abelian groups is zero. Restricting to this pointed neighbourhood leaves the stalk unchanged by Step 3 (now for schemes), so $(i_*A)_{\bar x}=0$.

source.place: Tag 04E5 (lemma-closed-immersion-push-pull), support clause; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04FX, proof, complement paragraph

proof.text: For a morphism $a:A\to B$ the two composites from a germ represented by $s$ on $W\times_XZ$ both give the germ of $a_{W\times_XZ}(s)$. The comparison maps commute with $a$ since restriction commutes with section homomorphisms. They preserve sums and zero for the same reason. This proves the stated naturality and the prescribed germ formula without any choice-dependent normalization.

lean.statement: theorem closed_pushforward_geometric_stalks {S : Scheme.{u}} {Z X : AlgebraicSpace S} (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@IsClosedImmersion) (Over.forget S)).relative yoneda i.hom.hom) : (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (b : Spec (CommRingCat.of Ω) ⟶ S) (z : yoneda.obj (Over.mk b) ⟶ Z.obj.obj), ∃ e : representableAbelianDirectImage i hi.rep ⋙ X.abelianStalk (z ≫ i.hom.hom) ≅ Z.abelianStalk z, ∀ (A : Sheaf Z.etaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (N : X.PointedEtale (z ≫ i.hom.hom)) (v : Over.mk b ⟶ ((representableEtaleBaseChange i hi.rep).functor.obj N.right).obj.left) (hz : yoneda.map v ≫ ((representableEtaleBaseChange i hi.rep).functor.obj N.right).obj.hom = z), v ≫ (representableEtaleBaseChange i hi.rep).projection.app N.right = N.hom.left → X.abelianGerm (z ≫ i.hom.hom) N ((representableAbelianDirectImage i hi.rep).obj A) ≫ e.hom.app A = Z.abelianGerm z (StructuredArrow.mk (CostructuredArrow.homMk v hz)) A) ∧ (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (b : Spec (CommRingCat.of Ω) ⟶ S) (x : yoneda.obj (Over.mk b) ⟶ X.obj.obj), (¬ ∃ z : yoneda.obj (Over.mk b) ⟶ Z.obj.obj, z ≫ i.hom.hom = x) → ∀ A : Sheaf Z.etaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}, IsZero ((X.abelianStalk x).obj ((representableAbelianDirectImage i hi.rep).obj A)))

reviewed_lean.note: Item statement matches the node clause by clause and agrees with Stacks 0DK1 (corrected direction), 04E5(2), 04FX, 03G2(4) and 03LR. Closed immersion uses Mathlib's ∀-square MorphismProperty.relative, equivalent to the project's ∃-form IsRepresentableWith. Direct image is sheafPushforwardContinuous along a base-change functor fixed by its pullback squares and projections, so it is not an arbitrary map. The stalk is colim over pointed étale charts, the germ is the colimit cocone, and the germ equation pins the natural iso (the induced point v is unique). The complement clause gives IsZero for every point not factoring through Z. Two new definition nodes are real constructions with no duplicate (side-live has only module direct images for spaces and scheme-only geometric stalks). Coefficients are AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} per the size convention. Edge cases checked: X empty, Z empty, i = id, nilpotent thickening, zero sheaf. lean.statement is verbatim in all three records; the item differs from live only by its lean record and the two new stmt_deps; docstrings carry source and blueprint ids; only sorry proofs. Not recompiled (no change). Advisory: the ∀ vs ∃ closed-immersion forms may need a bridge for citers.
